  PROBLEM: The runtime copy still permits bare time expressions in _limit_wait_forms. The wait_for pattern includes |{time} as an alternative, and retry_forms includes (?:reset_event|{time}) and (?:at|after|in|on|by) {time}. These were removed from the twin in review round 4 but not synced to the root copy.
  WHY: The Claude issue pickup executes .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py on every wake. Because the runtime script still accepts bare time expressions without tying them to the reset event, session summaries with instructions naming deadlines (such as "Usage limit reached. Please retry after 5pm." or "Usage limit reached. Wait until 5pm, then retry.") are classified as limit-only waits by is_limit_wait(), allowing the pickup to issue a resume trigger two minutes later instead of skipping the session as needs_input. This is the exact bypass review round 4 was meant to close.

This creates a declared-vs-effective capability gap: the documentation says the selector fails closed on bare times, but the runtime selector does not.
